findings.finding: Cancellation permits destructive process-group signaling when processStart(pid) is null: the mismatch condition is guarded by currentStart !== null. A null processStart/processGroup is therefore not treated as unknown identity; groupExists returns true when ps fails, so the path can proceed to signalGroup using only the recorded numeric PGID. This contradicts the stated “unknown identity; refusing destructive signal” contract and needs an explicit fail-closed identity rule before integration.

reconcile() is not protected by WorkerInstanceLock and performs no per-worktree/profile reservation acquisition before starting watchRecoveredAttempt. Two supervisor instances can independently reconcile the same journal and start duplicate heartbeat/settlement watchers. On restart, stale execution-lock directories intentionally cannot be auto-unlinked, but the recovered worker has no owner handle to reacquire/release them after the attempt settles, so physical reservations remain fail-closed for operator reconciliation.

A recovered watcher treats processStart(pid) === null as non-mismatch and may keep heartbeating when identity becomes unobservable; it should stop renewing and become ambiguous unless exact PID start and PGID remain verified. It also does not enforce the persisted wallTimeMs or outputBytes caps while a surviving process runs after supervisor restart, and the original stdout/stderr streams are no longer being observed. A restarted process could consequently outlive its allowed in-process caps.

The awaited-authorization replacement regression changes the selected Hermes home, but no test similarly replaces the enrolled root or worktree inode during authorization. Static rechecks include root/worktree identity, exact revision and clean Git state, but those two identity races are not directly exercised.

This runner denies ps/pgrep process enumeration. processStart/processGroup return null and the required temporary-executor suite cannot verify PID/PGID identities; the suite result is not a passing C05 validation. actual_flow: Codex hook session_id is normalized by extractAgentProviderSession and attached to the status event with paneKey, launchToken, tabId, worktreeId, and providerSession; connectionId is stamped on the remote-ingest path.
Renderer applyAgentStatus routes by paneKey and writes providerSession into agentStatusByPaneKey[paneKey]. Stable pane keys use tabId plus the durable layout leaf UUID.

terminalHandle is optional on AgentStatusIpcPayload but is not projected by the current local hook server toAgentStatusIpcPayload path; do not use it as required identity evidence until that path is explicitly populated.
session_identity_capture.capture_gap: sleepingRecordFromEntry copies paneKey/tabId/worktreeId/providerSession but omits originating PTY id, launchToken, and connectionId/runtime owner. PTY identity can be resolved from the exact stable leaf at capture time, but is not stored in the record.

findings: Quit captures in-memory provider sessions synchronously into sleepingAgentSessionsByPaneKey before building and synchronously flushing the workspace payload.

Schema verifies map key equals record.paneKey and validates provider id, but does not require record.tabId to equal the tab component encoded in a stable paneKey or validate that the record saved owner still matches a per-leaf PTY binding.

Hydration filters records by known worktree only; it separately restores terminalLayoutsByTabId and per-leaf ptyIdsByLeafId. The persisted provider session and PTY ownership hint are not one validated identity tuple.
Codex resume is selected from providerSession.key=session_id and emits codex resume <id>.

Terminal.tsx runs a startup sweep once per worktree per mounted renderer via a useRef set. Its duplicate claim key is worktreeId+agent+provider-session key/id, so equivalent session ids in separate worktrees are independent claims.

Pane cold-restore selects a stable-key record for that pane and uses its provider session while reattaching the PTY id stored for that leaf. Matching duplicate record aliases are cleared after the async transport connect resolves to a PTY id (or immediately on cold-restore reconnect), not before the operation starts.
codex_resume_selection.race_assessment: Two concurrent cold-restore pane mounts can both read the same provider-session claim before either transport.connect resolves and clears it; startup sweep and pane cold-restore also use separate ownership mechanisms. This is a concrete source-level race opportunity, but the reported two-process production sequence is not proven without an event trace.

findings: Stable paneKey is the correct durable tab+leaf identity; reconnectPersistedTerminals preserves per-leaf daemon session IDs and cold restore reads the matching leaf mapping.

The sleeping record itself has no PTY/runtime identity. recordPaneIsOwnedByPreservedPane checks that a stable leaf exists and has a restorable PTY hint, but does not prove that the PTY belongs uniquely to that providerSession record.
resolvePrimaryLayoutPtyId intentionally falls back to the active leaf or first leaf for legacy tab-level APIs; it must not bind split-pane provider sessions when an exact leaf mapping is available.

permanent_correction.recommendation: Bind the durable sleeping resume record to an exact execution owner (stable paneKey/tabId/leafId plus saved per-leaf PTY/session hint and runtime/connection identity); validate those fields as one tuple on capture, persistence hydration, and cold restore. Add one main-process atomic single-consumer resume claim keyed by provider/runtime identity and provider session id, with the chosen pane/PTy binding as owner, and acquire it before any spawn/await in both startup sweep and pane cold-restore. A stale or conflicting record must fail closed without launching another codex resume; keep stable leaf→PTY mapping authoritative for split panes and treat tab-level primary PTY only as an explicit single-pane legacy fallback.
permanent_correction.why: The current per-renderer startup ref is not a shared claim, claim identity is scoped by worktree, and pane-level duplicate records are cleared after spawn. native_read_preview_chunk_dto_proposed_n.native_race_contract: Use the existing DescriptorDirectoryTransport/helper process. For each chunk, open registered root no-follow and verify its native incarnation; traverse components by directory FDs with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW and named/opened parent identity checks. Final leaf open is O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC; immediately fstat and require regular file, registered-root device, exact expected identity/version and .md/.txt suffix. Compare fstat plus parent-relative no-follow stat before and after pread; recheck every parent descriptor/name and root path/incarnation before return. Close every FD in finally. No path-only Node read and no symlink/FIFO/socket/device/directory/mount traversal.
native_read_preview_chunk_dto_proposed_n.version: Canonical SHA-256 over a documented, length-framed tuple of rootId, root generation, root native identity/incarnation, file kind, dev, ino, sizeBytes, mtimeNs and ctimeNs. All full-width native integers remain canonical decimal strings across JSON. This is a stat-version token for ordinary change detection, NOT a content hash, integrity proof or protection against privileged restoration of metadata; contentDigestSha256 remains null.
native_read_preview_chunk_dto_proposed_n.limits: 16 KiB maximum raw chunk, 256 KiB maximum complete file, at most 16 sequential chunks; one in-flight chunk per session/principal and four active preview operations service-wide. Every complete JSON request/response must be measured and remain strictly below 64 KiB (16 KiB base64 is 21,848 characters plus bounded envelope). Use 1-second native-operation deadline, 5-second preview attempt deadline and short bounded session/lease TTL; enforce caps before any bytes are read.
native_read_preview_chunk_dto_proposed_n.process_cleanup: Reuse the current bridge singleton. Cancellation/deadline discards all buffered bytes and kills/cancels only its owned helper as the existing transport does. Do not release in-flight capacity while underlying work is pending; retain until it settles or child exit is confirmed. If cleanup is unconfirmed, refuse new preview/helper work; never spawn an overlapping helper.

assembly_and_privacy.assembly: Base64 must round-trip canonically and decode to the declared byte count. Render nothing until the final version, root and authorization checks pass; on any error discard the entire buffer.

design.freeBytes_semantics: Disk bytes, not RAM. This is an inference from CloudWorkerAssignment.minimumWorkingBytes, the queue failure reason Insufficient storage headroom, and C04 SystemMonitorVolumeStatus.freeBytes. CloudWorkerCapacitySample has no free-RAM field. WorkerCaps.memoryBytes is a separate per-job cap, compared with recipe maxCaps; it is not a free-memory measurement.
design.measurement: For the Linux worker host, sample filesystem bytes available to the service account from statfs/statvfs for the validated execution storage. On Linux prefer bavail * block size (available to unprivileged workers), use bigint arithmetic, reject unsafe/negative/overflowing values, and stamp only after all inputs are fresh. Bind the sample to the filesystem identity used by enrolled worktrees/profile homes/artifact destinations.
design.single_filesystem_requirement: The current reservation owner stores one scalar reservation total per device and the sample has no volume key. Safest minimal C05 design is to require all two-worker roots, worktrees, profile homes, state, and artifact/output destinations to share one filesystem identity before enrollment; otherwise change capacity samples and durable reservations to be keyed per filesystem. A device-wide minimum free-space scalar plus device-wide queue reservations is needlessly restrictive across filesystems and can still misrepresent which target volume is being protected.
design.externalReservedBytes: Sum only authenticated, outstanding non-C02 commitments for the same filesystem that are not already reflected as allocated bytes in the current statfs reading. Exclude C02 queue reservations because cloud_capacity_reservations is read transactionally and subtracted once by availableCloudWorkerBytes at claim and again at start-permit against the persisted current total. Never infer overlap from sample timestamps. Existing file allocation is already reflected in freeBytes and must not be subtracted again. If a complete fresh external reservation authority is missing, do not emit a sample or substitute zero; readiness/claim must fail closed.
design.receipt_contract: The existing worker-capacity.json reader requires a private regular JSON receipt bound to deviceId and a sample no older than 5 seconds, with strict numeric freeBytes, externalReservedBytes, safetyBytes, sampledAt. The currently absent producer must publish atomically in the service-owned cloud-workstation directory only after filesystem identity and external-reservation inputs are verified; an unbound device-only receipt is insufficient if enrollment can span filesystems.

design.api: createCloudWorkerCapacityCollector(options) captures a validated deviceId, approved execution-path set, safetyBytes, and a synchronous trusted readExternalReservations callback, returning a synchronous (requestedDeviceId) => CapacitySample reader. It does not persist another capacity receipt.
design.filesystem: Constructor checks every root, worktree, Hermes profile home, state directory, and artifact destination. Paths must be absolute/canonical, every component a non-symlink directory, and all captured bigint st_dev identities must match. Each read opens the selected worktree with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, verifies opened bigint dev/ino against the captured target, retains that descriptor through statfs via the verified Linux /proc/self/fd/<N> magic link, and rechecks every approved path after the final external-reservation callback before returning.
design.freeBytes: Linux only: verifies /proc and /proc/self/fd have PROC_SUPER_MAGIC, then reads bigint bavail * bsize from statfs through the open directory descriptor magic link; refuses non-Linux or unverified procfs, and rejects negative blocks, nonpositive block size, or values above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Darwin /dev/fd is not used or assumed equivalent.
design.externalReservations: Requires two synchronous strict snapshots bound to device and filesystem identity, complete all_non_c02_reservations coverage, equal current revision, <=5-second freshness, and identical revision/reservedBytes across the read. Stale, unknown, incomplete, misbound, changed, or thrown authority refuses the sample; no zero fallback is present.
design.reservationAccounting: Returns freeBytes from statfs and externalReservedBytes from the authoritative non-C02 snapshot. It does not subtract C02 SQLite queue reservations; existing admission/start-permit logic remains their sole owner and subtraction point. Already allocated space is represented by statfs and is not subtracted again.
design.scope_limits: This module is not wired into production bootstrap/main/config and does not implement the external reservation authority or verify Hermes credentials/enrollment. The local Darwin run used the injected descriptor-statfs test seam; the Linux-only default procfs test is included but skipped on Darwin and remains for ROOT isolated Linux proof. No worker/provider/live configuration was read or changed.
